text:
alex: heads up — noticed a p99 tail spike starting ~10m after the 2.3.1 rollout. only affects requests with >1500 tokens. logs: https://redwood.internal/logs/rollout/2.3.1 (see trace ids 0x9a1/0x9a2)
kevin: any config changes in the rollout? microbatching or kernel selector thresholds?
jia: microbatch default was bumped 8->16 in the rollout to improve throughput for short seqs. kernel selector also changed: we added a fallback cutoff for fused-kernel at seq_len>=1024 to avoid OOM on some cards.
alex: quick numbers from last 30m window (prod-us): p95 +12ms, p99 +72ms, 99.9th +220ms for long prompts. throughput is up ~8% overall. The pain is tail latency on long-context calls that also trigger tool calls.
monica: profiler snapshot shows repeated KV cache invalidations inside tool-calls — when a tool call happens we drop the session entry then rebuild a new KV chain, which forces expensive full-attention recompute on resume. snippet from trace: ```
TRACE 0x9a1: recv request seq=1800 -> choose kernel=fused if seq<1024 else generic_matmul
KV_CACHE: miss session=usr-42 ctx_len=1800 -> allocate new segment
TOOLCALL: external -> pause_inference, persist_state=false
RESUME: rebuild_kv_chain cost=96ms
```
perf-bot: summary: "p99_regression: +72ms (long-ctx, tool-loop), root_causes: [microbatch_slew, kernel_fallback, kv_rebuild]"
kevin: hypothesis: combination of larger microbatch and kernel cutoff pushes more long-ctx requests to generic kernels, plus batching across tool-call boundaries creates outlier generation durations. two quick mitigations to test: 1) dynamic microbatch cap based on ctx_len (cap=8 if ctx_len>1024), 2) avoid batching requests that have active toolcall flags (batch-splitting by tool_call metadata). config example: ```json
{"batcher":{"max_microbatch":16,"dynamic_caps":[{"ctx_min":1024,"cap":8}] ,"batch_by": ["user_id","tool_call"]}}
```
alex: can we reproduce in staging? need a deterministic harness that simulates long prompt + tool loops (tool latency ~50-200ms).
jia: i'll run a microprofile with synthetic workload (seq lens 1200..2000, toolcall probability 0.35, tool RT=80ms). steps: 1) deploy canary with microbatch cap and kernel selector debug logging, 2) run 10k sessions with random tool loops, 3) capture KV hit/miss and kernel_choice per step. commands: ```bash
./perf-harness --canary=eng-runtime/canary/microcap --sessions=10000 --seq-min=1200 --seq-max=2000 --tool-p=0.35
```
monica: also add a KV pin flag on resume path so that when a session hits tool loop we mark and prevent eviction for X requests. rough patch: `kv.pin_on_toolcall = true` — avoids rebuild thrash at cost of memory. will prototype.
deploy-bot: canary created: canary-id=canary-kvcap-1789991122, link: https://redwood.internal/deploys/canary-kvcap-1789991122
kevin: if repro shows kernel fallback is primary, we should consider lowering the fused-kernel cutoff and invest in a streaming-kernel for >1k tokens rather than generic matmul. also monitor microbatch latency tail when batching spans tool boundaries.
alex: action items: jia -> run microprofile and upload results; monica -> prototype kv.pin_on_toolcall; kevin -> spec dynamic microbatch cap + batching-by-tool_call; i'll coordinate canary and gate the rollback if p99 > baseline+50ms. tagging @kevin @jia @monica. :thumbsup: 
monica: noted, will post a summary + perf plots when prototyping is ready.
alex: thanks — syncing in 2h to review results.
